Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-SAT and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-p0l44vc9 && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set.

Construction (standard "clause gadget" reduction):

Given a 3-SAT instance with ``num_vars`` variables and clauses C_1..C_c,
build a graph with one vertex per literal occurrence, i.e. 3 vertices for
each clause.  Vertex ``3*i + j`` corresponds to the j-th literal of clause i.

Edges:
  * Within each clause, connect all three vertices in a triangle.  Any
    independent set therefore contains at most one vertex per clause.
  * Between clauses, connect two vertices whose literals are contradictory
    (v and -v).  This forbids choosing an assignment that makes both a
    literal and its negation true.

Set ``k = c`` (the number of clauses).

A satisfying assignment yields an independent set of size c by picking, in
every clause, one literal that is true.  Conversely, an independent set of
size c must pick exactly one vertex per clause (triangles), and the
contradiction edges guarantee the chosen literals are mutually consistent,
so they define a satisfying assignment.  Hence the graph has an independent
set of size at least c iff the formula is satisfiable.

Edge cases:
  * No clauses: k = 0, empty graph -> k <= 0 is yes, matching satisfiability.
  * k is never negative here, and k <= n always (n = 3c >= c), so the
    target's k <= 0 / k > n special cases never distort the answer.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Map a 3-SAT instance to an Independent Set instance."""
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    num_clauses = len(clauses)

    n = 3 * num_clauses
    edges = []

    # Map each vertex to its literal.
    literals = []
    for clause in clauses:
        for lit in clause:
            literals.append(lit)

    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            same_clause = (i // 3) == (j // 3)
            contradictory = literals[i] == -literals[j]
            if same_clause or contradictory:
                edges.append([i, j])

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": num_clauses}
EOF
